dedupe_keys.name: project nexus connecting domestic instant payment systems for cross border payments bis innovation hub

description: Project Nexus was a BIS Innovation Hub project to connect domestic instant payment systems into one network so that cross-border payments can reach recipients within 60 seconds in most cases. Instead of each operator building custom links to every other country, a system makes a single connection to the Nexus platform and reaches all countries on it, improving the speed, cost, transparency of and access to cross-border payments. It was run by the BIS Innovation Hub Singapore Centre from 2022 with the central banks of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand, after a 2021 blueprint. Through successive phases it delivered a proof of concept, reported in March 2023, a prototype, and in July 2024 a scheme and governance framework, commercial model and technology blueprint. In 2025 the central banks of India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand set up Nexus Global Payments to run it live, and the BIS handed the project over, marking it concluded. Coverage is these Asian countries. The reports are free on the BIS site. Caveats: the page summarises results, and technical and resilience detail sits in the reports. For simulation it describes a hub-and-spoke network linking national payment systems, useful in network flow and resilience models of cross-border payments and of how an outage at one node would affect others. It is related to the TARGET2 outage case study record in this catalogue.
